about: Pet teams: several Markdown pets that work together on one job, in one folder, for someone who wants the agents without installing Astra's PetOS. Read by scripts/pet-teams-20261120.mjs, which writes pet-teams/ on npm run build. Each pet's name, job, tools and picture come from the registry (the same data as its Markdown pet); this file holds only the team, each pet's role in it and the read-only checks it may suggest. Astra, 2026-11-20: "people that need stuff, they might not want to download my operating system at all ... I can just sell them my agents". Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), 2026-11-20.

teams.title: Security Team
teams.for: Watch your own PC and your own home network, the way Astra's security pets watch hers: one group for the network, one for the PC. They look and explain; you decide and make every change yourself.

groups.name: Network
groups.about: Is the network healthy, what is on it, what can reach in, and what radios are near.

pets.role: The network's health: loss, latency, DNS and routes. Says whether the network was fine at a given moment, so a problem is put in the right place (the router, the provider, DNS or a website).

checks.look: The router and DNS server this computer uses
Loss and latency to the router (put the router's address from the step above in place of ROUTER)
How long a DNS answer takes
Whether the internet answers (one connection, no data sent)
The hops to a website, when something is slow or down
The network adapter in use and its speed

pets.role: Ports and devices: which ports are open on this computer, which program owns each, who is connected and from where, which devices this computer has seen on the home network, and what to close. Security checks only on your own computer and network.

checks.look: Every port this computer listens on, and the program that owns it
Who is connected to this computer right now, and from where
The devices this computer has seen on the home network (nothing is scanned)
Whether the firewall is on
What the router lets in from the internet: you open the router's own page and read its port forwarding and UPnP lists aloud or as a screenshot

pets.role: The radios nearby: Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth devices, and any that are new or unknown. Only its security role is part of this team; the rest of its job is still being chosen.

checks.look: Wi-Fi networks in range, with their security
The Wi-Fi network this computer is on
Bluetooth devices paired with this computer

pets.role: Remote access and VPNs: which ways in from outside are switched on (remote desktop, SSH, a VPN or tailnet), whether each is meant to be, and how to keep the ones you use private.

checks.look: VPN connections set up on this computer
Whether Remote Desktop is switched on (0 means on)
The tailnet, when Tailscale is installed

groups.name: PC
groups.about: What runs on the computer, what its logs say, whether it is patched, and what happened when something goes wrong.

pets.role: What runs on your PC: every program and what it is, what is safe to stop, the leftovers that keep running after a window closes, and what starts at sign-in.

checks.look: The programs using the most processor time, with where each runs from
What starts at sign-in
Scheduled tasks that are switched on
Who signed a program you are not sure about (put its path in place of PATH)

pets.role: The logs: errors and crashes in the system's own logs, failed sign-ins, and anything that repeats. Reads logs; never clears them.

checks.look: The newest errors in the application log
checks.windows: Get-WinEvent -LogName Application -MaxEvents 200 | Where-Object LevelDisplayName -in 'Error','Critical' | Select-Object -First 30 TimeCreated,ProviderName,Message

checks.look: The newest errors in the system log
checks.windows: Get-WinEvent -LogName System -MaxEvents 200 | Where-Object LevelDisplayName -in 'Error','Critical' | Select-Object -First 30 TimeCreated,ProviderName,Message

checks.look: Failed sign-ins (needs an administrator window on Windows, sudo on Linux; ask first)

pets.role: When something looks wrong: a case with a timeline of what happened when, from the other pets' findings, with a fingerprint (SHA-256) of every file kept as evidence. It never changes or deletes what it looks at.

checks.look: A fingerprint of a file kept as evidence (put its path in place of PATH)
Recent sign-ins and restarts, for the timeline
Files in the sign-in startup folder, with when each changed

pets.role: Patches: which security updates Windows, the drivers and the apps are still missing, and whether the antivirus is on and up to date. It lists; you install.

checks.look: The newest Windows updates installed
Apps with a newer version (this only lists them)
Whether Microsoft Defender is on and its signatures are fresh
